newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan chip makers see no major impact from EU move.
newsitem.headline: Japan chip makers see no major impact from EU move.

text.p: Japanese semiconductor makers said on Tuesday that they did not expect any major impact from the European Commission's reintroduction of minimum prices on dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips.
"We think that the move would not have a major impact on our chip business," a spokeswoman for Fujitsu Ltd said.
Some makers, however, said that the EU's move might hurt European chip users as they may have to pay higher prices.
A spokesman for Hitachi Ltd said: "We don't expect any direct influence on our business but we think European users may face some problems to some extent."
The EU said on Monday it was reintroducing minimum prices on DRAM chips originating in Japan and Korea with immediate effect.
The EU imposed anti-dumping duties on Japanese exporters in January 1990 and later on Korean exporters. The measures were suspended 21 months ago due to the rise in DRAM prices.

Japan's Kyodo news agency said that the EU decided to reintroduce the system because DRAM prices had fallen dramatically to below the cost of production of most producers, again hurting EU producers, and also because of the expiry on Monday of the 21-month suspension.

"Japanese makers are not dumping their chips in the European market," an official of the Electronic Industries Association of Japan (EIAJ) said. "The EU renewed the system due to the expiration of the 21-month suspension," he said.
"The EU's law allows up to a 21-month suspension so the system was revived," an official of another chip maker said.
DRAM chip prices fell sharply last year on the global market due to excessive supply, Japanese chip makers said.
But the prices have recently started rebounding due chiefly to an improvement in supply-and-demand conditions amid strong demand from memory board makers, the makers said.
